newsitem.title: INDIA: Thousands of Hindu devotees stranded on pilgrimage.
newsitem.headline: Thousands of Hindu devotees stranded on pilgrimage.

text.p: Some 4,000 Hindu pilgrims on a Himalayan pilgrimage were stranded on Saturday due to heavy snowfall in northern India, a police spokesman said.

"Around 2,500 are stranded near Sheshnag Lake and another 1,000 near Panjtarni," a police spokesman told Reuters in Jammu, the winter capital of the state of Jammu and Kashmir. "Another 500 are in between."
He said the pilgrimage to the sacred mountain cave of Amarnath in Jammu and Kashmir had been indefinitely suspended until the snow stopped. No casualties were reported.
At least 214 pilgrims died last year after bitter winds and heavy snow lashed the trail to Amarnath, located 12,500 feet (3,846 metres) above sea level, some 330 km (200 miles) northeast of Jammu.
The police spokesman said snow was falling heavily at Mahagunus Top, a mountain pass at 14,800 feet above sea level.
He said the pilgrims had erected tents along the route, where the temperature had fallen to five degrees Celsius (41 degrees Fahrenheit).
Community kitchens set up to feed the devotees on the annual pilgrimage were operating, but it was not immediately clear how long their food stocks would last.
Sheshnag Lake is 306 km (184 miles) northeast of Jammu, and Panjtarni lies 13 km (eight miles) further along the route to Amarnath.
Since the pilgrimage began on July 16, more than 24,000 pilgrims have visited the cave, where they worship an ice stalagmite believed to be a symbol of Lord Shiva, the Hindu god of regeneration.
The 5,000-year-old cave's chief priest says he expects 120,000 pilgrims to visit Amarnath this year.
